stem.text: A parallel beam of light of wavelength $600\,\text{nm}$ is incident normally on a diffraction grating.

The distance between adjacent slits in the grating is $2.0 \times 10^{-6}\,\text{m}$. A screen is placed parallel to the grating, at a distance of $1.50\,\text{m}$ from the grating. **Third-order** diffraction maxima are observed at the two ends of the screen, as shown.

stem.alt: Ray diagram: a beam of light of wavelength 600 nm incident on a diffraction grating, with rays to a screen 1.50 m away; third-order maxima labelled at the two ends of the screen. Marked not to scale.

stem.text: What is the distance between the two ends of the screen?
